newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya says aircraft flew to Ghana despite U.N. ban.
newsitem.headline: Libya says aircraft flew to Ghana despite U.N. ban.

text.p: Libya said on Wednesday a Libyan aircraft had flown an official Libyan delegation to Accra despite a 1992 United Nations ban on its international flights.
The official Libyan news agency JANA reported the flight but did not say when the aircraft landed in the Ghanaian capital.

JANA, monitored in Tunis, said an adviser to President Jerry Rawlings greeted the Libyan foreign ministry delegation at Accra airport. The delegation was visiting Ghana on an official visit, the agency said.

Libya has told the Security Council it is no loner subject to the U.N. flights ban after it gave permission for a balloon to overfly its territory last week. A U.N. sanctions committee source on Tuesday rejected the claim.

The United Nations imposed sanctions on Libya including bans on international flights after it refused to hand over two Libyans indicted by in the United States and Britain for their alleged role in the bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988 killing 270 people.

Libya has broken the flight ban on several occasions -- it flew Moslem pilgrims to Saudi Arabia in 1995 and 1996 and a Libyan-registered aircraft flew Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi to Cairo and back to attend an Arab summit in June 1996.
